prospect.name: Jeroen Lodder
prospect.occupation: Manager / Programme Manager, Learning & Development, at a Dutch employer with twelve locations; working 50-60 hours a week, reduced to 40-45. Formerly a lecturer and student coach at HAN University of Applied Sciences. Has resigned effective end of September and has not yet found a new role.
prospect.family_status: Lives with his boyfriend and their dog. Primary unpaid carer for his mother since he was 10, roughly 24 years; care was 24-hour from February to mid-April after she fell and hit her head, now reduced to every other week. His boyfriend was assaulted this summer by a group of teenagers, struck in the head with a bicycle chain, and has not recovered.
prospect.training_background: Trained seriously from 15 to 19 — volleyball two to three days a week plus two to three gym sessions, including kettlebells, sandbags and medicine balls during the European functional-training wave. Was 85-86 kg at an estimated 17-18% body fat. A slipped disc at 19 ended it. Currently walks 6-8 km a day with the dog, over 300 km a month, restarted volleyball last year and intends to play twice a week from September, and holds a gym membership as a condition of the Dutch CLI programme. Uses a standing desk and already does hourly movement breaks and wall stretches. Has watched all of Trevor's videos.
prospect.medical: Born with a congenital upper-gastrointestinal malformation, not surgically corrected until age three, during which he could take only liquids and was chronically hungry; he reports that he has never had a sensation of fullness since — 'if I let loose, I can eat up to 18,000 calories. I tested it. I tried. And I still didn't cause a feeling of full.' Slipped disc at 19, after which he went from 86 kg to 130 kg. Lost 130 kg to 86-88 kg in three months on the Dukan protein diet and turned jaundiced — 'I was completely yellow... because my liver couldn't handle such a weight loss in such a small amount of time.' Currently 103.6 kg, peak 105.8 kg in March, BMI over 30. Diagnosed: autism, high intelligence, bulimia nervosa, PTSD from childhood. Suspected but undiagnosed ADHD. Cannot tolerate pork. Diagnosed irritable bowel syndrome and confirmed slow bowel transit — a seven-day marker-pill study showed the first pill still present at day eight. Suicide attempt at 21; intrusive suicidal thoughts have returned to at least weekly, which he and his family doctor both consider abnormal, and he is on a waiting list for mental health treatment. Two weeks of severe insomnia at the time of the call. Enrolled in the Dutch CLI (combined lifestyle intervention) programme via health insurance and seeing a dietitian on his family doctor's referral.

signals: In the middle of an active health crisis rather than recovering from a past one: weekly suicidal ideation, an active eating disorder and a mental-health waiting list, all disclosed on the call.

Training is explicitly framed as part of fighting it, and both he and his family doctor treat it that way — 'if I can get my body up to better standards and getting fitter and healthier then she and I both agree that those dark thoughts will already tamper and be less frequent'.

The rep named the archetype himself and the prospect confirmed it: 'you're literally fighting for your life right now, for a better life' / 'Yeah, for a better life. I think that's a better way of saying it.'
Diverges from the archetype in one important way: he had hard price resistance, which prehab fighters usually do not. He is the rare case of extremely high intent with no capacity to pay.
Overlaps with the_rebuilder — he was fit at 15-19 and wants that body back — but the deciding factor is that the health event is live, not historical.

There's a lot of medical information about it. So my question is, does Trevor have any knowledge of that? Because that's very important for me to know.
objections.rep_response: Answered honestly rather than closing over it: 'I would lie to you right now if I would say yes, definitely he has knowledge on that, because I don't know that, probably he has, but I'm not going to tell you right now that yeah, for sure he has.' The prospect thanked him for it. The rep then fell back on customisation — 'this is not a regular program for everybody, everything is tailored to your schedule, your needs, your lifestyle'.

tiers.note: Primal University community product, $199 per month, cancellable at any time — includes a three-month kettlebell programme, movement guidance, meal and nutrition protocols, and a weekly live training and Q&A with Trevor. Not one-to-one and not tailored.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Offered in principle only — 'if you're not in a position to do it upfront, that is fine too... if we could potentially find a way to split that up, we can.' No structure was built because the prospect's ceiling of €200 a month made a split unworkable.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Asserted without terms: 'the full transformation takes six months. There's a guarantee on that also.' Never specified, and never referenced again.

prospect_financials.note: Ceiling stated as €200 per month, and lower if his next job pays less. Describes his current salary as well above the Dutch average but is already paying for the CLI programme and a dietitian. Notes that Dutch credit cards must be repaid immediately or carry roughly 14% monthly interest, so the upfront-credit-card route is structurally unavailable to him.

The rep disqualified rather than discounting: 'with $200 a month, that would definitely be a stretch for us. It's not doable.'

Counter-evidence on finality: the prospect said 'yes and no' when asked whether he was still considering the six-month option, and both sides agreed to revisit once his new job is settled after 15 October.

A downsell is live but unclosed — he agreed only to receive an email about the $199/month Primal University and wants a week to decide: 'I want to take at least a week to think about it and to think what's best for me.'
He named a competing use for the same money: 'am I going to my local physician and ask them to give me one-on-one training?'
Nothing was paid, no link was sent, and no follow-up call was booked — only an email and an open invitation to stay in touch.
outcome.next_step: Rep to email the price options including the $199/month Primal University. Prospect to decide within about a week between that, a local physiotherapist for one-to-one training, or nothing. Revisit the six-month programme after he secures a new role, likely after 15 October.

notable.note: The most clinically loaded transcript in the batch and, in one respect, the best-handled. The prospect disclosed diagnosed bulimia nervosa, autism, childhood PTSD, weekly suicidal ideation against a prior attempt, IBS with confirmed slow bowel transit, a congenital condition that has left him with no satiety signal at all, and prior liver damage from a crash diet — and the rep still presented an intermittent-fasting nutrition protocol built on the premise that 'it's virtually impossible to overeat when you're eating real food', which is precisely the mechanism this prospect's body does not have. No clinician was contacted and no safeguarding step followed the suicide disclosure. Against that, the rep did two things right that no other call in this batch does: he told the truth when asked whether Trevor has relevant expertise — 'I would lie to you right now if I would say yes' — and he disqualified on affordability at €200/month instead of inventing a tier. This is also the first call in the corpus to document the Primal University product and its price, $199/month cancellable, and the first to surface a structural market problem: Dutch credit cards must be repaid immediately or carry about 14% monthly interest, so the entire upfront-credit-card close is unavailable in the Netherlands.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion throughout, worst in the first two minutes where the rep's and prospect's opening lines are entirely swapped, and again across the nutrition and accountability sections where the rep's presentation is attributed to the prospect. Several long passages run together without punctuation or speaker breaks, including the whole suicide-disclosure exchange from about 00:21:32 to 00:25:07. Role was resolved from content. The recording itself is complete and ends on a normal sign-off. The prospect's full name appears in the speaker label and is the only place it appears.
